hero.titleLine2: and ChatGPT, Cursor, any MCP client
hero.lead: Give your AI agent your Outlook.com, Hotmail, Live or MSN inbox. Sign in with Microsoft, approve access once, and read, search, send, reply, schedule and organize mail from every MCP client with one URL.
hero.meta1: Sign in with Microsoft, no app password
hero.answer: Yes. mcpemails is a hosted MCP server that connects a personal Microsoft account, an address ending in outlook.com, hotmail.com, live.com or msn.com, through Microsoft Graph. You click Connect with Microsoft, sign in, and approve access on Microsoft's consent screen, where MCP Emails appears as a verified publisher. There is no app password and no IMAP setting to enter, and no administrator is involved for a personal account. Paste one URL into Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any MCP client and the agent can read, search, send, reply, forward, schedule and file your mail. One inbox is free, forever.

method.title: How Outlook.com connects: Sign in with Microsoft
method.body: Outlook.com connects through Microsoft Graph with OAuth 2.0, not over IMAP. You sign in on Microsoft's own page and approve a short list of permissions: read and change mail (Mail.ReadWrite), send mail (Mail.Send), stay connected (offline_access) and your basic profile and email address. Your Microsoft password is typed only into Microsoft's page and never reaches us. To disconnect, delete the inbox in mcpemails, or remove MCP Emails from the apps that have access to your Microsoft account.

setup.p: Sign up for mcpemails, no card required. The free plan connects one inbox, forever.

setup.h: Choose Outlook and connect with Microsoft
setup.p: In the dashboard, open Connect inbox, pick Outlook, and click Connect with Microsoft.
Sign in on Microsoft's page with your Outlook.com, Hotmail, Live or MSN address and approve the permissions. You land back in the dashboard with the inbox connected.

setup.h: Paste the MCP URL into your AI
setup.p: Drop https://mcpemails.com/api/mcp into Claude, Cursor or ChatGPT, authorize, and your agent has the inbox.

gotchas.h: App passwords and IMAP passwords do not work, which is why this uses Microsoft Graph
gotchas.p: Microsoft ended Basic authentication for personal accounts connecting from non-Microsoft apps from 16 September 2024, and the Outlook.com IMAP service now offers only OAuth. Many older guides still tell you to generate an app password; it cannot log in to mail any more. mcpemails does not use IMAP for Outlook.com at all: it signs in with Microsoft and talks to Microsoft Graph, so there is no password to create and no server setting to get wrong.

gotchas.h: hotmail.com, live.com and msn.com addresses are the same service
gotchas.p: The mail behind all of those domains is one Microsoft consumer service. An old hotmail.com address connects exactly like an outlook.com address created yesterday: choose Outlook and sign in with that address.

gotchas.h: A Microsoft account without an Outlook mailbox is refused
gotchas.p: If the Microsoft account you sign in with has no Exchange Online mailbox behind it, Microsoft Graph has nothing to open, so mcpemails refuses the connection and tells you so. If that address's mail is hosted on another server, connect it with IMAP instead.

gotchas.h: A brand-new Outlook.com account may be blocked from sending for a while
gotchas.p: Microsoft's anti-abuse systems can temporarily stop a newly created Outlook.com account from sending when it sends many messages in a short time. This is a restriction on the Microsoft account, not a connection fault, so reconnecting the inbox does not change it.

limits: Outlook organizes mail in folders, including nested folders. The label tools are Gmail-only, but an automation's label action applies an Outlook category to the message.

Microsoft Graph cannot combine a text search with the unread, attachment, flagged or date filters. When a search includes text, those filters are not applied, and the result says which ones were left out.
Sending carries up to 10 MB of attachments per message; downloading attachments and forwarding originals work up to 25 MB.
The self-hosted version connects over IMAP and SMTP only. Signing in with Microsoft is part of the hosted service.

faq.a: Yes. Connect your Outlook.com mailbox to mcpemails by signing in with Microsoft, paste one MCP URL into Claude, and Claude can read, search, send, reply, forward, schedule and file your mail. The same URL works in ChatGPT, Cursor and other MCP clients.

faq.q: Does it work with Hotmail, Live and MSN addresses?
faq.a: Yes. They are the same Microsoft consumer mail service as outlook.com, so they connect the same way: choose Outlook in the dashboard and sign in with that address.

faq.q: Do I need an app password or IMAP settings?
faq.a: No. mcpemails connects Outlook.com through Microsoft Graph after you sign in with Microsoft, so there is no app password to create and no IMAP or SMTP server to enter. An app password would not work anyway: Microsoft stopped accepting passwords from non-Microsoft mail apps on personal accounts in September 2024.

faq.q: What can my AI do in Outlook.com?
faq.a: Read, search, send, reply and forward; work with drafts; create and use folders, including nested ones; move, copy and archive; flag; delete to trash or permanently; send up to 10 MB of attachments per message, and download attachments or forward originals up to 25 MB; schedule sends; run automation rules; and manage your signature.

faq.q: Is this the same as connecting a work Microsoft 365 account?
faq.a: The sign-in is the same, the approval may not be. A personal account needs no administrator. A work or school Microsoft 365 account often needs an IT admin to approve MCP Emails once for the organisation first. When that is the case, the dashboard gives you an approval link to send to your IT admin, and they do not need an MCP Emails account to use it.

faq.q: Is my email stored on your servers?
faq.a: No. Messages are fetched live from Microsoft for each request and handed to your AI client. The OAuth token from your Microsoft sign-in is encrypted at rest and message bodies are not retained. Deleting the inbox in mcpemails ends the connection straight away, and you can also remove MCP Emails from the apps that have access to your Microsoft account.
